updates.text: Updated the chat-latest snapshot, which points to the latest model available in ChatGPT for Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise users. We recommend leveraging the GPT-6.2 model family for production API usage, but feel free to use this model to test the latest improvements for chat use cases. The und

Released Healthcare model configurations for the Responses API, pairing select OpenAI models with a harness tailored to clinical questions. When the model uses web search, it searches a dedicated index of medical sources.

Use GPT-6.2 Astra for demanding reasoning and coding tasks, or GPT-6.2 Sol for everyday coding and agent workflows. Both models support the Responses API and Chat Completions. Tool calling requires the Responses API.

GPT-6.2 changes how the Responses API preserves reasoning when you edit a conversation’s prefix and how it handles the top-level instructions field. See the GPT-6.2 migration guide for details and recommended updates to your integration.

Choose a two-hour or eight-hour background completion window in the Responses API public beta. Model token rates are 30% lower than Standard for the two-hour window and 40% lower for the eight-hour window.
New models will not support Flex processing. Flex remains available on supported models while the beta winds down.

Approved organizations can use the OpenAI CSAM Image Classifier at no cost to help prioritize images for human review. The model returns separate signals for potential child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and potential AI-generated CSAM.

Released GPT-Image-2.6 Sunburst and GPT-Image-2.6 Flare for image generation and editing, with adjustable complexity, SVG generation, and animated GIF generation. Added markup-guided editing for supported GPT-Image-2.5 and GPT-Image-2.6 models.

You can now update the tools in an existing session in the Agents API public beta. Updates replace the full tool list. Function tools and MCP servers change on the next model call; built-in tools change by the next turn.

Added opt-in experimental time awareness. Set experimental.time_awareness to true to give the model periodic current-time reminders. It is disabled by default. See the agent configuration reference for compaction and experimental settings.

Incognito conversations. Set incognito to true on the call_perplexity_computer call that starts a conversation. Answer tools need followup_uuid. answer_question, confirm_action_approve, and confirm_action_deny now require followup_uuid and fail without it. Read it from the event’s interactive object or from read_thread. These tools now return as soon as the answer is sent, with task_status: "working". Call re
Embeddings API: pplx-embed-v2-context-9b and pplx-embed-v2-context-0.6b

Three request formats. Send requests in the OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, or Anthropic Messages format. Every model supports all three. The API is stateless, so send the full conversation on every request.
Model routing. Set model to perplexity/auto and a decision model picks the model for each request, from the default policy or from routes you define in a routing object. See Routing and Reliability.

Access by usage tier. xAI, open-weight, and Google Gemini Flash models work at every usage tier. OpenAI models, google/gemini-4-neon, google/gemini-4-hydrogen, and most Anthropic models require Tier 1. anthropic/claude-opus-5, anthropic/claude-opus-5-5, anthropic/claude-fable-5, anthropic/claude-fab
Decisions API: pplx-decider-v1.3, pplx-decider-flash-v1.3, and locate questions
Analytics API: credit-usage response update

This page lists the latest features and improvements for Microsoft 365 Copilot. It includes changes that are generally available (Current Channel for Microsoft 365 apps) and specific to each platform.
Copilot features are introduced using a safe deployment model, gradually rolling out to a subset of users within a tenant before expanding across the organization.
Share custom organizational attributes with Microsoft 365 people experiences [Web]
We're introducing a new capability in Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service that enables organizations to share selected custom organizational attributes with the Microsoft 365 people store.
Why: The change allows organizations to select custom organizational data to make available in Microsoft 365 people experiences.
Review existing custom attributes in Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service.
Determine whether Microsoft 365 experiences would benefit from including any custom attributes.
Configure app access settings in Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service to select custom attributes to make available to Microsoft 365.
Why this matters: Organizations can enable new organizational data scenarios for Microsoft 365 while controlling which attributes are visible to Microsoft 365 experiences.
Personal impact: Users can access additional organizational information in Microsoft 365 experiences when their organization chooses to share it.
